thread.title: Cuba Experiences Total Blackout Amid Ongoing Energy Crisis
thread.title_full: Cuba Experiences Total Blackout Amid Ongoing Energy Crisis

author: Associated Press
title: Cuba Experiences Total Blackout Amid Ongoing Energy Crisis
text:
• A total blackout occurred in Cuba on Wednesday, attributed to aging infrastructure and fuel shortages at power plants.
• This blackout is the latest in a series of outages reported this year.
• The Ministry of Energy and Mines indicated that the outage may be linked to a malfunction at one of Cuba's largest thermoelectric plants.
• Argelio Abad, vice minister of the ministry, stated that an erroneous message warning of overheating led to the disconnection of the thermoelectric plant.
• Officials are working on building a microsystem to provide electricity to essential services.
• Crews are focused on restoring power to hospitals, food production plants, and other high-priority businesses.
• Prime Minister Manuel Marrero urged Cubans to trust that electricity would be restored gradually.
• Some residents, like 65-year-old Mayté García, expressed concerns about prolonged outages affecting food preservation.
• Havana, the capital with a population of approximately 2 million, remained calm, with residents seeking essential items before dark.
• Traffic lights in the city were non-operational, and many social and cultural activities were suspended.
• Gas stations continued to operate, providing fuel during the blackout.
• Internet service in Havana was reported to be slow or intermittently dropping in some areas.
• The ongoing power outages have led some residents to prepare for such events, with some owning small power plants.
• Earlier in the week, an outage affected Cuba's eastern region, impacting areas from Las Tunas to Guantánamo.
• In February, the government suspended classes and work for two days due to electricity generation shortages.
• Cuba's energy crisis has worsened in recent years, exacerbated by sanctions that limit foreign currency for fuel and equipment repairs.
